rules.sentence: Differentiate between partial, intermediate, and complete atrioventricular septal defect based on anatomical and clinical characteristics.
Determine the appropriate timing and indications for surgical repair of an atrioventricular septal defect based on the patient's presentation and defect type.

Coordinate comprehensive postoperative care with the interprofessional healthcare team, including monitoring for complications such as atrioventricular valve regurgitation, arrhythmia, and residual shunting, and support transition to long-term follow-up in congenital heart disease clinics.
Partial AVSD typically presents with an ostium primum atrial septal defect, separate AVVs with a common junction, an inlet ventricular septal defect, and a cleft mitral valve.
In contrast, complete AVSD features a common AVV, an ostium primum atrial septal defect, and an unrestricted inlet-type ventricular septal defect.
